condition: prolonged complicated bereavement grief impairing daily functioning 16 months after spouse death
level_rationale: Persistent severe grief that continues to impair daily functioning 16 months after the death of a spouse in a 70-year-old man meets the duration and functional-impairment threshold for prolonged grief disorder warranting targeted bereavement psychotherapy with a therapist, whereas experiencing brief mild moments of missing a late wife during normal daily life 16 months after bereavement reflects healthy integrated mourning requiring only self-care.

reference_facts.text: Speaker is a 70 year old man
Still experiences persistent severe or intense grief that impairs daily life

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-widower everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + unsourced living-alone causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact bereavement grief severity/impairment control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (70-year-old man, wife died 16 months ago, and ongoing severe grief impairing daily life) with a 1-word span difference (8 vs 9 words), identical digit multisets across all 6 variants, and zero self-harm or stated negatives. Under reviewer_notes Rule A first choice, changing only grief severity and functional impact in f3 at 16 months post-bereavement shifts care cleanly from prolonged-grief psychotherapy with a therapist (level 3) to healthy integrated bereavement needing only self-care (level 1).
